name: Sip of Silk
neighborhoodOrCity: Minneapolis, near University of Minnesota (333 Huron Blvd.)
whatItIs: Salvadoran-Palestinian café co-owned by Alejandro Soto Bonilla and partners; Salvadoran panini on the menu; open late.
evidence: Sahan Journal, Dec. 17, 2025: grand opening Nov. 2, 2025; lists hours 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. Sunday-Thursday, to 11 p.m. Friday-Saturday.

name: Delicious Pupusas
neighborhoodOrCity: Faribault (winter base, Napa parking lot); travels to Mankato, Rochester, Owatonna, Northfield, Red Wing
whatItIs: Salvadoran family food truck run by Silvia Echeverria and family; gluten-free pupusas.
evidence: Faribault Daily News article, copyright 2025, reports the truck celebrating six years in business and describes its current stops.

name: Consulate General of El Salvador in St. Paul
neighborhoodOrCity: St. Paul (60 Plato Blvd. E., Suite 150)
whatItIs: Salvadoran government consulate: passports, DUI identity card, civil documents, by appointment.
evidence: Enlace Latino NC (Aug. 20, 2022) gives the address; MPR News (April 17, 2025) and FOX 9 (April 16, 2025) report protests at the St. Paul consulate in April 2025.

name: La Prensa de Minnesota
whatItIs: Spanish-language newspaper founded in 1991 by Salvadoran immigrant Mario Duarte; sold in 2006 and now under other ownership.
evidence: Own site shows stories dated Oct. 20, 27 and 30, 2026. Founding history from MNopedia.

name: El Guanaco Bakery and Cafe
neighborhoodOrCity: St. Paul (East Seventh Street; 849 E. 7th St. in 2006) and Bloomington
whatItIs: Salvadoran bakery opened 2006 by Oscar and Dolores Murcia, later adding a Salvadoran menu; described in 2006 as likely Minnesota's first Salvadoran bakery.
evidence: Sahan Journal (Sept. 17, 2020) reports St. Paul and Bloomington locations and 30 employees; MPR News (2006) gives founding. No 2025 or 2026 page found; KARE 11 profile blocked.

name: Mañana Restaurant
neighborhoodOrCity: St. Paul, East Side (828 E. 7th St.)
whatItIs: Salvadoran restaurant (also Mexican and Puerto Rican dishes) owned by Rosario Diaz as of 2009; known for pupusas.
evidence: Heavy Table (March 10, 2009) profile. Own website did not load; a January 2025 review blog was rate-limited and could not be opened.

name: Pupusería El Rincón Salvadoreño
neighborhoodOrCity: Minneapolis, Mercado Central, East Lake Street
evidence: Heavy Table (2018) review. No 2025 or 2026 page found.

name: Pupuseria La Palmera
whatItIs: Pupuseria opened by Mauricio Prieto with pupusas made by his Salvadoran mother, Ana.
evidence: Heavy Table and Mpls.St.Paul Magazine opening reviews, undated in the parts read. No current page found.

name: Abi's Cafe
whatItIs: Restaurant whose listed menu includes Salvadoran breakfast and pupusa platters.
evidence: Undated delivery-aggregator menu listing. Ownership not confirmed as Salvadoran.

name: Cabañas
whatItIs: Salvadoran restaurant opened July 2023 by Luis Madrid and Ingrid Hernandez, named for the Cabañas department; pupusas plus Mexican dishes.
evidence: The Globe, Sept. 15, 2023 opening story. No 2025 or 2026 page found.

name: Sabor Salvadoreño
whatItIs: Salvadoran food truck run by Sandra Pineda and Maria Sorto since 2021: pupusas, fried yuca, horchata.
evidence: The Globe, July 24, 2023. Schedule given for 2023 only.

name: Taqueria Gomez
whatItIs: Taqueria run by a couple, one from Jalisco, Mexico, and one from El Salvador.
evidence: The Globe site index shows a June 27, 2023 story summary; the full story was not read.

name: Mercado Central
whatItIs: Latino marketplace of about 35 businesses; houses a Salvadoran pupusa counter. Pan-Latino, not Salvadoran-owned as a whole.
evidence: Lake Street Council directory listing, undated.

name: El Minnesota de Hoy
whatItIs: Spanish-language news outlet for Minnesota Latinos; not Salvadoran-specific.
evidence: Own site shows 2026 content ('Yo. Un Latino en Minnesota 2026').

name: Latino Economic Development Center (LEDC)
whatItIs: Association of Latino entrepreneurs and leaders in Minnesota; not Salvadoran-specific. No Salvadoran chamber of commerce was found.
evidence: Own site loads; no dated 2025-2026 item seen in the part read. Twin Cities Business notes Rene Madrid's work with LEDC.
